newsitem.title: USA: JONES TO BUY N.M. CABLE SYSTEM FOR $223MLN.
newsitem.headline: JONES TO BUY N.M. CABLE SYSTEM FOR $223MLN.

text.p: Jones Intercable Inc said Thursday it agreed to buy an Albuquerque cable television system from Cable TV Fund 12-BCD Venture for about $223 million.
Jones, which is the Cable TV venture's general partner, said it would use its existing credit lines to pay for the acquisition. It expected to close the deal in the first quarter of 1998.
The cable television operator said the Albuquerque system serves about 112,800 viewers.

"The acquisition of the Albuquerque system is yet another step toward our goal of becoming an owned-asset company, rather than primarily a management company," said president James O'Brien in a statement.
Jones Wednesday said it planned a secondary offering of 7.8 million shares to partially pay for its buying an Independence, Mo., cable system from one of its managing partnerships.
The company's shares closed at 12-10/16 Wednesday.
